The 10-name growth book is led by three secular AI compounders (CRWD, AMD, MSFT) benefiting from Microsoft alone reporting Azure at +43% and a $90B quarter, flanked by META's FCF machine, two energy names (MPC/COP) capitalizing on the cheapest sector by forward P/E (14.12x) and ISM Prices Paid re-acceleration, TMO in the Healthcare rotation 'emerging' quadrant, SPGI backed by Ackman's $1.06B initiation, ETN for AI power infrastructure, and NEM as a commodity inflation hedge within equities. New addition vs. prior book: MSFT replaces PLTR (MSFT's Oct 27 Azure catalyst and 4/4 beats is a structurally cleaner risk/reward than PLTR's -20% YTD and 84x GAAP forward PE); COP replaces NET (sector diversification — COP adds energy value chain breadth; NET at -3.2% off high after +41% 3M is near-term extended). PANW was considered but excluded from growth book to maintain the IT sector cap at 3 names; its Nov 12 earnings is a strong re-entry trigger if CRWD consolidates. The dominant risk being underwritten today is the September NFP print (releasing at 8:30 ET this morning) — a beat above 120K payrolls or wage acceleration above 0.4% MoM would materially harden November hike pricing, compressing the forward P/E from 19.3x toward 19.0x and widening credit spreads further, hitting SNOW, PLTR, and high-leverage names hardest while validating the energy and gold overweights.
diversificationNote: The growth book spans 7 GICS sectors: Information Technology (CRWD, AMD, MSFT — max 3 per rule), Communication Services (META), Energy (MPC, COP — complementary downstream/upstream split), Health Care (TMO), Financials (SPGI), Industrials (ETN), and Materials (NEM); CRWD and MSFT share cloud/software exposure but are differentiated by cybersecurity vs. hyperscaler end-markets. The defensive sleeve covers four distinct exposures: physical gold (GLD — inflation/fiscal shock hedge), broad dividend quality equity (SCHD — value/yield factor tilt countering AI multiple risk), quality conglomerate with $365B cash fortress (BRK.B — quality defensive and option on market dislocation), intermediate-duration Treasuries (IEF — recession hedge without TLT's fiscal blow-up risk), and consumer staples (KO — pricing power ballast), deliberately avoiding TLT given the 30Y yield at a 19-year high and fiscal term premium risk.
